benchmark_kind: cost of candidate-level secure ranking, as an alternative to oblivious graph scanning
scope_warning: Single host, three local parties, one query, synthetic zero-valued scores. The noise draw is a PLACEHOLDER (sint.get_random_int(16)), not a calibrated discrete Laplace or Gumbel sampler; a real differentially private mechanism costs more than measured here. Scores are dummy because the circuit is data-independent, which makes the cost figure valid but the privacy claim unmeasured. No DP guarantee is claimed or implemented.
question: The implemented design obliviously scans the whole federated graph for every query, which relation_paged_multiaxis.json shows is linear in graph size and near-quadratic in owner count. This probe asks what it would cost to compare only CANDIDATES across parties, moving the graph-sized work out of MPC entirely.

design_probed.idea: Each party scores its own subgraphs locally in plaintext (free, no MPC, no obliviousness overhead) and submits its top m as secret shares. MPC does only the cross-party comparison: add noise to each candidate score, then take an exact top-k of the noisy scores.
design_probed.topk_algorithm: naive O(k*n) select-and-suppress; a sorting network or oblivious heap would be cheaper, so these figures are an upper bound
design_probed.what_it_deliberately_avoids: any oblivious read over the graph; there is no directory scan and no page pool in this circuit at all

comparison_against_the_implemented_desig.the_asymptotic_point: The candidate-level cost is INDEPENDENT of graph size. 192 candidates cost the same whether the federation holds 10^2 or 10^8 entities, because the graph-sized work happens locally in plaintext at each party. Cost becomes O(parties * candidates) instead of O((1 + frontier) * entities * relations * parties).

the_tradeoff_this_buys_and_costs.buys: Removes the graph-size and owner-count scaling walls simultaneously. Makes real-dataset evaluation feasible.
the_tradeoff_this_buys_and_costs.costs: Local plaintext scoring requires each party to learn enough about the query to score against it. The implemented design hides the query from data owners; this design does not, unless query privacy is recovered separately (for example by routing on a coarse semantic bucket rather than the query itself, which src/semantic/lsh.py and src/orchestration/private_semantic_routing.py already sketch).
the_tradeoff_this_buys_and_costs.verdict: This is a threat-model trade, not a free optimization: query privacy against data owners is exchanged for many orders of magnitude of scalability. It should be presented as an explicit design axis with both endpoints measured.

what_this_does_not_show: Any differential privacy guarantee; the noise is a placeholder.
Any real dataset, WAN, or multi-host result.
That local plaintext scoring is acceptable in the target deployment; that is a threat-model decision.
An optimized top-k; the naive O(k*n) selection measured here is an upper bound.
